edges.description: Autoantibody production generates the circulating receptor-directed IgG lesion.
At high titer, the receptor-directed antibodies predominantly antagonize insulin action.
At low titer, the same receptor-directed antibodies can act as insulin mimetics.
At high antibody titer, receptor blockade impairs downstream insulin signaling, driving extreme insulin resistance and hyperglycemia.
Low-titer receptor agonism can drive spontaneous, sometimes intractable hypoglycemia.
Impaired insulin action produces the defining extreme insulin-resistant state.
Loss of insulin action produces severe, often refractory hyperglycemia.
Severe loss of insulin action is associated with marked acanthosis nigricans.
In affected women, the severe insulin-resistant state can produce hyperandrogenism.
Failure of insulin action produces a hypercatabolic state with severe weight loss.

nodes.description: Fasting or intractable hypoglycemia without exogenous insulin, occurring when antibody titers are low and the autoantibodies act as receptor agonists. Historically a major driver of mortality. A rare subgroup has isolated hypoglycemia with suppressed, rather than elevated, insulin and may have a delayed association with aggressive lymphoma.

evidence.snippet: Isolated hypoglycemia with low insulin forms a rare subgroup of type B insulin resistance. These patients lack the common characteristics of hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia/insulin resistance. Furthermore, while coexisting autoimmune disease is commonly observed, there is potentially an association with aggressive lymphoma, the onset of which may be delayed.
